messages.text: Do the two layouts have different coverage ?
I’ll compare the retained coverage samples for both layouts, including where the missed crossings occur.

Yes. They have the **same nominal radii and barrel length**, but the phi-tilted layout has fewer missed sensor crossings in the identical coverage sample.

| Track model | Tangential layout: missed crossings | Phi-tilted layout: missed crossings |
|---|---:|---:|
| Straight | 0.713% | 0.122% |
| Positive charge, \(p_T=1\) GeV | 0.620% | 0.115% |
| Negative charge, \(p_T=1\) GeV | 0.622% | 0.095% |

These percentages count **eligible layer crossings**, rather than track efficiency. The curved tracks use a 4 T field.

Both layouts have zero sampled misses more than 100 mm from the barrel ends. The remaining losses occur near the ends, so neither demonstrates complete hermeticity.

The tilted alternative also has **8,064 modules versus 7,952**—112 more, or 1.4%. Its improvement therefore reflects both the changed placement and the increased module count; this is not a tilt-only comparison.
